levelMapping: Ladder: SWE I -> SWE II -> Senior I -> Senior II (often written SSE/SSE2) -> Staff 1/2. SWE II ~ Google L4 (2-5 YOE); Confluent Senior maps to Google L5 / Meta E5 per Confluent employees on Blind. At ~3.3 YOE expect SWE II, with Senior I reachable (India posts show 3.5-5 YOE candidates interviewing for SSE/Senior I). SSE2 loops add a second system-design round and per a 2025 reject report require at least one strong-hire in design.

process.summary: Confluent recycles a small, stable bank of practical multi-part coding problems rather than broad LeetCode: nearly every 2024-2026 loop contains some mix of the windowed-average/TTL key-value store, word-and-phrase search over documents, Sudoku validate-then-solve, tail -n of a huge file, and the variadic function-signature matcher. The loop is recruiter screen -> (HackerRank OA for some) -> 60-min technical phone screen ('qualifier', run working code on CoderPad/HackerRank) -> virtual onsite of 2 coding rounds + 1-2 system-design rounds + an engineering-values round + a hiring-manager round, then team matching and a role-sell call. Design rounds are the real senior bar: multiple candidates passed all coding rounds and were rejected purely on design, where interviewers scrutinise API design (verbs, response codes, pagination), SQL/data modeling and unbounded-scale reasoning. Interviewers rate 0-4 Google-style and a packet is reviewed centrally.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, motivation, logistics, level and timezone choice (India candidates can be scheduled with India or US/EMEA interviewers). Recruiters send per-round prep emails that name each round's focus, e.g. 'practical file operations: solve problems using file APIs' or 'network mesh: algorithms and data structures'.
rounds.probes: CTC expectation, notice period, which team/req.

rounds.name: Online assessment (HackerRank)
rounds.what: 1-3 coding problems around LC-medium. A Sep 2026 report had 3 problems in 60 min; a Mar 2025 senior candidate got a single LC-medium with 15 test cases. Campus/new-grad OAs were 100 min, 3 problems (binary search, TSP-style, MST). An OA-bank problem: rank songs by pairwise user preferences (majority beat-counts with tie-breaks).
rounds.probes: Clean working code against test cases; roughly 80% pass bar. Senior/referred candidates sometimes skip straight to the phone screen.

rounds.name: Technical phone screen ('qualifier')
rounds.what: One practical multi-part problem implemented and RUN on CoderPad/HackerRank, usually from the classic bank: variadic function-signature matcher, time-window KV store with get_average, word lookup in a file, wildcard match (older). Problem grows in parts.
rounds.probes: Follow-ups on time complexity and concurrency/locking; edge cases; they expect you to extend code, not rewrite it, as parts are added.

rounds.name: Coding round 1 (machine coding / practical)
rounds.what: Practical implement-and-run problem, most often the documents word search -> ordered phrase search -> AND/OR boolean queries progression (inverted index), or tail -n over a huge file with constrained file APIs.
rounds.probes: Clean class structure, tokenization rules, incremental extension, build-vs-query cost, memory limits, streaming output. One London reject was for writing duplicated code even though the solution worked.

rounds.name: Coding round 2 (DSA)
rounds.what: LC-medium algorithmic problem, overwhelmingly Sudoku validator extended to Sudoku solver (backtracking); also combination-sum-to-target staged variants, grid shortest-path with monster costs (0-1 BFS -> Dijkstra), heap problems.
rounds.probes: Memory-efficient validation (counts via hashmap), printing which row/col/box fails, input validation, pruning in backtracking, complexity stated unprompted.

rounds.name: System design (1 round for SWE II/Senior I, 2 for SSE2)
rounds.what: Product-infra designs from a small bank: URL shortener, RSS/news-feed aggregator (Feedly-like), temporary email service, podcast publish/subscribe feed, distributed key-value store. Not always diagram-driven: several rounds were almost entirely API design + SQL schema.
rounds.probes: REST vs RPC, exact endpoints/verbs/response codes, pagination (cursor vs offset), table design and indexes, fanout-on-read vs fanout-on-write, capacity math (RPS, memory, servers), dedup/idempotency, TTL expiry at scale, uniqueness guarantees (Bloom-filter false positives get challenged).

rounds.name: Operations-at-scale / specialty deep dive (team-dependent)
rounds.what: Some loops (e.g. Cloud/Traffic teams) add a round on running systems: detecting bottlenecks, LB access logs, multi-region routing, replica lag, slow-query analysis, IaC/Terraform, monolith-to-microservices; one Jan 2026 'super day' was intense grilling on Linux internals (shell -> fork/exec, filesystems, procfs, containers vs VMs).
rounds.probes: HLD first, then 'how do you actually do it in cloud'; OS-level mechanisms named precisely.

rounds.name: Engineering values round
rounds.what: Behavioral round mapped to Confluent values: exceeding customer expectations, taking initiative in hard situations, challenging legacy decisions, mentoring, handling ambiguity in large systems, volunteering/teamwork. Scheduled only after technical rounds pass.
rounds.probes: Real engineering stories with depth, not rehearsed leadership-principle answers; they dig into specifics.

rounds.name: Hiring manager round
rounds.what: Project deep dive + behavioral: why Confluent, disagreements with teammates, most challenging work, a bug you introduced and how you found it, customer interactions, strengths. For role-fit mismatches (e.g. DevProd vs distributed-systems aspirations) the HM probes whether you actually want this team's work.
rounds.probes: Architecture of your current system, decisions and trade-offs you personally made.

rounds.name: Team matching + role-sell call
rounds.what: After a hire decision: conversation with a specific team about their work and culture, then an offer/role-sell call.
rounds.probes: Mutual fit; can add 1-3 weeks to the timeline.

process.indiaNotes: Confluent hires SWE II/Senior in Bengaluru and remote-India; the India loop uses the same question bank as US/EMEA (several India candidates matched questions reported from London/US). India candidates often choose interviewer timezones; coding/screen rounds tend to be India-staffed, design rounds sometimes AMER/EMEA. Referrals move fast (recruiter calls within hours-to-days). India-specific friction in 2025: a global hiring freeze (~Apr-Jul 2025) left at least one India candidate with a cleared loop waiting on an offer letter. Campus (IIIT/IIT) hiring uses a separate OA + DSA + pure-concurrency loop.
process.timeline: Referral to recruiter call: hours to ~3 weeks. Screen to onsite: ~3 days-2 weeks. Full loop commonly 3-6 weeks; with values round, packet review, team matching and offer it can exceed 2 months (one SSE2 report: 'expect >2 months').
tips: Grind the Confluent classics, not breadth: windowed-average/TTL KV store, documents word+phrase search (inverted index), Sudoku validate+solve, tail -n of a huge file, variadic signature matcher. The bank is small and has been stable since ~2022.
Every coding problem is multi-part: do not rush part 1, and write code you can extend; interviewers add constraints (AND/OR queries, variadic flags, arbitrary costs) on the spot.
Write clean, de-duplicated, runnable code from the first draft — one senior candidate got a no-hire for duplicated code despite a working solution and an acknowledged cleanup plan.

Design rounds are the senior filter: candidates with strong-hire coding feedback get rejected on design. Drill API design details (verbs, status codes, headers, cursor pagination), concrete SQL schemas with indexes, and fanout trade-offs.
In design, defend uniqueness/scale guarantees rigorously — Bloom-filter hand-waving (false positives, unbounded growth) was called out in the temp-email question.
Prepare concurrency as a follow-up skill: 'make it thread-safe', locking granularity, scheduler-based TTL cleanup (min-heap of expiries) vs lazy cleanup.
Know your language's file APIs cold (seek/read-n-bytes/file-size, reading backwards in blocks) — one full round is often file manipulation.
Values and HM rounds carry real weight and are scheduled only after technicals; bring specific stories (bug you shipped, disagreement, mentoring, customer issue).
Clarify the level up front: SWE II vs Senior I changes the number of design rounds and the bar.
Ask the recruiter for the per-round prep email and read it literally — it names each round's focus and maps 1:1 to the known bank.
process.notes: IBM acquisition closed ~March 2026: ~950 non-R&D layoffs, the standalone careers site was shut (apply via IBM), and mid-2026 candidates report a disorganized pipeline (interviewers missing Teams logins); R&D hiring continued but expect turbulence and verify the req is real. OA platform: HackerRank; onsite coding on CoderPad/HackerRank with runnable code expected. Feedback is 0-4 Google-style with central packet review; two lean-hires or a design no-hire ends SSE2 loops. Language is normally your choice (Java/C++/Python/Go all seen); one Mar 2025 candidate was restricted to JavaScript for a specific (frontend-adjacent) team, and some candidates sign NDAs. A dedicated concurrency round existed through ~2023 (job-scheduler style) and survives in campus loops; for experienced hires concurrency now appears as follow-ups inside coding rounds. 'Network mesh' appears as a round name in recruiter prep emails (algorithms/DS focus, likely graph connectivity) but no candidate has published its content. No reports of Kafka-internals trivia (ISR, consumer groups, rebalancing) being asked in SWE loops — design rounds test the underlying concepts (partitioning, replication, delivery guarantees, offsets) instead.

sources.title: Confluent SWE — HackerRank, Sudoku, machine coding, DevProd values (PracHub)
Confluent Senior I — variadic screen, phrase search, podcast design (PracHub)
Confluent Senior — passed both codings, failed both designs (PracHub)
Confluent interview coming up — IBM acquisition thread (Blind)
What to expect in the Confluent system design interview (DesignGurus)

dsa.title: Time-window key-value store with get_average (windowed average)
dsa.statement: Implement a key-value store where entries expire after a fixed window (e.g. 5s or 1h): put(key,value) records the value with the current timestamp, get(key) returns the value only if not expired, and get_average() returns the mean of all currently non-expired values. Calls arrive with non-decreasing timestamps. Optimize get and get_average toward O(1) using a running sum plus an ordered structure (deque/linked list) to evict expired entries.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: lazy cleanup vs a scheduler driven by a min-heap of expiry times; what a get on an expired key does; thread safety. Related LC: 981 Time Based Key-Value Store, 2622 Cache With Time Limit, 1797 Design Authentication Manager.
dsa.evidence: Confluent's signature phone-screen/qualifier: Oct 2024 SSE2 phone screen, Aug 2024 Bengaluru coding round 2, 2024 qualifier (reconstructed in comments with exact op trace), Blind 'windowed average' 2022.

dsa.title: LRU cache with TTL and constant-time average
dsa.variant: Confluent's version adds to LC 146: entries carry a TTL/timestamp, and get_average() over currently active values must also be O(1) (running sum updated on insert/replace/evict). Follow-ups: TTL expiry without scanning, dynamic capacity, thread safety (lock striping), vector values, numeric overflow.
dsa.evidence: Round 1 of Apr 2025 India SSE loop (add with timestamp, get, average of active values); 'modified LRU cache' phone screen in the 2024 London senior loop; PracHub bank item dated Jan 2026.

dsa.title: Valid Sudoku
dsa.variant: Asked memory-efficiently (count maps, not 27 sets), with extras: report WHICH row/col/box is invalid, validate digits are 1-9, handle partially filled boards. Almost always extended to Sudoku Solver in the same round.
dsa.evidence: The most-reported Confluent coding question: Sep 2026 phone round, Aug 2026 onsite, May 2025 SSE2, Dec 2024 onsite, Oct 2024 SSE2, Aug 2024 Bengaluru (with the row/col/box reporting twist), 2024 London (no-hire over duplicated code).

dsa.title: Sudoku Solver
dsa.variant: Follow-up to Valid Sudoku in the same round; plain backtracking suffices but they probe pruning and recursion structure. Boards given have exactly one solution.
dsa.evidence: Paired with the validator in Sep 2026, Aug 2026, May 2025, Dec 2024, Oct 2024 and Aug 2024 reports.

dsa.title: Function signature matcher with variadic/optional parameters
dsa.statement: A registry stores function signatures: name, ordered parameter-type list, and an is_variadic flag (last parameter may repeat one or more times); some versions add optional parameters. Given queries of ordered argument-type lists, return all functions that accept each call. Exact string type matching, no coercion. E.g. funB=['int','int','int'] variadic matches ['int','int','int','int']. Solvable with a hashmap of exact signatures plus prefix handling, or a trie; expect ~1e4 functions and queries.
dsa.variant: Staged: exact matching first, then optional args, then the variadic flag. Interviewers accept hashmap or trie (one Aug 2026 interviewer steered to hashmap). Variadic 'Integer... args' style parsing in the May 2025 version.
dsa.evidence: The standard technical-screen question: Aug 2026 screen ('the classic isVariadicFunction'), Feb 2026 screen, May 2025 SSE2 phone screen, Aug 2024 Bengaluru coding round 1 with worked examples.

dsa.title: Word search then phrase search across a list of documents (machine coding)
dsa.statement: Given a list of documents (id + text), build a search component. Part 1: find_word(word) returns ids of documents containing the word (whole-word match; decide tokenization/case). Part 2: find_phrase(phrase) returns documents where the phrase's words appear in the same order (clarify: adjacent or not — both variants asked). Expected: inverted index word -> doc ids, extended with per-occurrence positions to verify order, including repeated words ('to be or not to be').
dsa.variant: Part 3 twist (Aug 2026): queries with AND/OR operators over words — clarify precedence, map to set intersection/union. Follow-ups: add/delete documents, ranking, sharding the index, words within k positions.
dsa.evidence: Confluent's flagship machine-coding round: Sep 2026, Aug 2026 (with AND/OR), Apr 2025 India round 3, Dec 2024 round 1, Oct 2024 coding round 1, 2024 London coding round 1, Blind Sep 2022.

dsa.title: Search words and phrases in a file larger than memory
dsa.statement: A text file has one sentence per line and may be much larger than memory. Design an API to find every line containing a word, then every line containing an exact multi-word phrase. Compare a one-off streaming scan against building a persistent positional inverted index for repeated queries; define tokenization, result format (line numbers/byte offsets), and how updates become searchable.
dsa.variant: File-backed variant of the documents search; asked as a talk-through in a Jan 2026 screen where a hashmap-index answer sufficed but needing hints cost the candidate. Follow-ups: relevance ordering, sharding, compressed input, atomic index swaps.
dsa.evidence: Screen of the Jan 2026 'Linux-heavy super day' (Senior, Cloud Traffic team); PracHub bank item.

dsa.title: Implement tail -n: last N lines of a very large file
dsa.statement: Return/print the last N lines of a log file in original order without loading the whole file. Start with language file methods, then optimize: read backward in fixed-size blocks (or forward with a bounded deque of N lines), handle chunk boundaries, trailing newline, files with fewer than N lines, n=0. One version restricts you to three file APIs — get file size, read k bytes at pointer, move pointer by delta — and requires pseudocode that streams output to stdout rather than buffering the result.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: buffering vs file-pointer-offset trade-offs, non-seekable streams, follow mode (tail -f), file rotation, decoding multi-byte encodings safely. The 2024 'LLD round' framing emphasized memory optimization and low-level memory constructs while reading a huge file.
dsa.evidence: Apr 2025 India round 2 (print last N lines of a log file), Feb 2026 onsite coding round 1 (with the 3-API pseudocode part), 2024 senior offer loop onsite 2, Apr 2026 paired with the monster-grid problem, multiple PracHub bank entries.

dsa.title: Minimum monster cost path in a grid (0-1 BFS -> Dijkstra)
dsa.statement: A grid has start S, exit E, empty cells (cost 0), monster cells (cost 1 to enter) and walls. Moving 4-directionally, return the minimum total monster cost from S to E, or -1 if unreachable (grid up to 300x300; 0-1 BFS). Follow-up 1: return one minimum-cost path as coordinates, preferring fewer steps among ties. Follow-up 2: each monster has its own non-negative cost up to 1e9 (separate cost matrix) — switch to Dijkstra.
dsa.variant: Asked in the same round as tail-of-file (second half).
dsa.evidence: Onsite coding round reported Apr 2026 (PracHub, 'Implement Tail and Find Monster Cost').

dsa.title: Constrained monster traversal on a directed graph with energy and potions
dsa.statement: Directed graph of n rooms, each with monster hp[i] >= 0; you start at s with energy E, entering a room subtracts its hp, energy may never go negative. Part A: does a survivable path to t exist? Return the path (DFS over simple paths with energy pruning). Part B: potions in some rooms add energy on first entry; find a path to t maximizing distinct rooms visited while staying non-negative, or -1.
dsa.variant: Justify why simple paths suffice when hp >= 0, and what changes with potions.
dsa.evidence: Technical-screen bank item on PracHub (updated Jun 2026).

dsa.title: Pick numbers summing to a target: existence with negatives, one and all solutions
dsa.variant: Confluent's staged version goes well beyond LC 39: (1) existence check, all-positive (subset-sum DP); (2) existence with negative numbers — explain which pruning/bounds break; (3) return one solution (trace back through the DP); (4) return all solutions without duplicates; (5) optimizations (bitset DP, dedup, meet-in-the-middle for 40 elements with values up to 1e9). Clarify reuse rule and target 0 / empty set first.
dsa.evidence: Reported Oct 2026 on PracHub; Combination Sum is also in Confluent's LeetCode tag.

dsa.title: Process pod logs with global increments and pop-min
dsa.statement: Process a stream of pod-log operations supporting: insert a value, increment ALL stored values by a delta, and pop/return the minimum. The trick is a min-heap plus a running global offset so bulk increments are O(1): store value-minus-offset in the heap and add the offset back on pop.
dsa.evidence: Technical-screen bank item on PracHub (updated Jun 2026).

dsa.title: Rank songs by pairwise user preferences
dsa.statement: n users each give a permutation ranking of m songs. Song x 'beats' y if a strict majority of users rank x before y, or exactly half do and x < y. A song's beat count is how many distinct songs it beats; output all songs ordered by beat count desc, ties by smaller id. Precompute per-user position arrays for O(1) preference checks; compare 2*count vs n to avoid floats.
dsa.evidence: Online-assessment bank item on PracHub (updated Jun 2026).

dsa.title: File tail + sensor health (heartbeat liveness)
dsa.statement: Two-part onsite round: (1) tail a large file via buffer/pointer manipulation (as above); (2) given a stream of sensor heartbeat timestamps, track which sensors are healthy/alive within a time window and report liveness — a hash map of last-seen times plus window reasoning.
dsa.evidence: Onsite bank item on PracHub (updated Jun 2026).

dsa.title: Debug and fix a Quicksort, then improve pivot selection
dsa.statement: Given a buggy Quicksort implementation, find and fix the bugs, then harden pivot selection against O(n^2) worst cases — discuss randomized pivot, dual-pivot and median-of-three.
dsa.variant: Confluent's occasional debugging-style round (round 5 of a 6-round SSE2 loop).
dsa.evidence: May 2025 SSE2 loop (strong-hire coding feedback); commenters confirm it recurs.

dsa.title: Explain Linux: command execution, filesystems, procfs, containers vs VMs
dsa.statement: Knowledge deep-dive (infra/cloud teams): trace what happens from shell input to a running command (parsing, PATH lookup, fork/exec, wait, exit status; why cd must be a builtin); how ls/pwd/ip get their data; path traversal, inodes, file descriptors, directory vs file permissions, why /proc is not a disk directory; containers vs VMs via namespaces/cgroups vs hypervisors, with trade-offs.
dsa.variant: Follow-ups: pipelines, TOCTOU races, container escape in a shared-kernel model, user namespaces.
dsa.evidence: The Jan 2026 Senior 'super day' (Cloud Traffic) was largely this grilling; PracHub bank item.

dsa.title: Explain variadic functions across two languages
dsa.statement: Knowledge companion to the signature matcher: explain variadic functions in two languages of your choice (C/C++, Go, Java, Python) — calling conventions, how the callee accesses args, type safety (generics vs raw varargs), boxing/reflection overhead, forwarding varargs. Often paired with implementing a small type-safe variadic logger.
dsa.evidence: Technical-screen bank item on PracHub (updated Jul 2026), tied to the recurring variadic screen.

dsa.title: Thread-safe LFU-like cache
dsa.variant: Asked as 'an LFU-cache-like thing'; after the single-threaded version works, make it thread-safe if time remains (lock granularity probed).
dsa.evidence: Round 4 of the Dec 2024 SSE onsite.

dsa.title: Wildcard pattern matching (phone screen, older loops)
dsa.variant: Phone screens through ~2022 were LC-hard (wildcard match; another report: hashmaps + KMP). Since 2024 screens shifted to the practical bank, but hard DP/string remains possible.
dsa.evidence: Blind Sep 2022 screen report; Feb 2022 Blind loop had an LC-hard screen (hashmaps+KMP).

design.title: Design a URL shortener
design.prompt: Design a reliable URL shortening service: create + redirect APIs, short-code generation, storage, caching, expiration.
probes: capacity math they actually make you do: RPS, memory, number of servers
DB and cache sharding; hot/popular links as cache hot keys
collision-safe code generation; custom aliases; code-space migration
expiration and deletion consistency across caches/replicas
pros/cons of multiple approaches rather than one design
abuse controls, negative caching, async analytics off the redirect path
design.evidence: Design round of Dec 2024 SSE onsite; Design 1 of Oct 2024 SSE2 loop (explicit focus on scalability, sharding, resource calculations); PracHub bank item updated Jul 2026; Feb 2022 loop's 'first question in Grokking' is the same prompt.

design.title: Design an RSS / news-feed aggregator (Feedly-like)
design.prompt: Design a service where users subscribe to sources/publishers; ingest articles on a schedule, dedupe, and serve each user a personalized feed. Explicitly API- and schema-first: name the tables, columns, indexes and endpoints.
probes: REST vs RPC and adapting the API to mobile clients
cursor-based pagination (OFFSET breaks mid-scroll)
concrete relational schema + the index behind each hot query
fanout-on-read vs fanout-on-write vs hybrid; celebrity-source hot spots
dedup/idempotency with unreliable RSS guids; conditional fetches (ETag)
SQL queries written out, not hand-waved
design.evidence: Design 2 of Oct 2024 SSE2 loop (Feedly, API design + data modeling); Feb 2026 onsite design 1 (news-feed aggregator, 'mostly API design'); 'Newsfeed generation' round in a Feb 2022 loop; PracHub RSS item (Apr 2026).

design.title: Design a temporary (disposable) email service
design.prompt: Design a TempMail-style service: generate inboxes on demand, receive mail, let users read messages; addresses expire after a fixed window (5-10 hours in reports).
probes: generating human-looking usernames at huge daily volume so external sites don't reject them
usernames must NEVER be reused with no deletion — uniqueness checks at scale; Bloom filters get challenged on false positives and growth
expiry mechanism and storage lifecycle (per-message TTL, cleanup jobs)
SMTP/MX ingress, spam/abuse controls, rate limiting
access control and validation of addresses
design.evidence: May 2025 SSE2 HLD round 2; Feb 2026 onsite design 2 (candidate failed on uniqueness-at-scale); PracHub hard bank item.

design.title: Design a podcast publishing/subscription service
design.prompt: Creators publish episodes; listeners follow shows and see new episodes in a feed. Cover the upload/processing path for audio and delivery of new episodes to followers.
probes: no architecture diagram expected in one version — API design (verbs, response codes, headers), SQL queries and data modeling instead
fanout-on-read vs fanout-on-write vs hybrid, walked through explicitly
shows with millions of followers vs tiny shows; who pays, publisher or reader
audio blob vs metadata storage; reliable 'published' event
episode deletion, late followers, scheduled publishing, push notifications at scale
design.evidence: May 2025 SSE2 HLD round 1 (podcast service, API/SQL focused); Aug 2026 Senior I onsite round 3 (fan-out discussion).

design.title: Design a distributed key-value store at scale
design.prompt: Design a globally distributed KV store optimized for read-heavy workloads, down to OS-level performance (threads vs async I/O, memory), storage layout/compaction, partitioning, replication, caching and consistency.
probes: partitioning/sharding, key distribution, rebalancing
replication + caching write/read paths, coherence, TTL, invalidation
consistency models and CAP trade-offs as client-visible guarantees
failure detection, leader election, recovery
hotspot mitigation, backpressure, rate limiting
write amplification and compaction trade-offs
design.evidence: PracHub bank item (May 2026); a 1point3acres 2025 guide says the Confluent process 'centers on a distributed key-value store design round'; 'design a data store (key, value)' was the design round in a Sep 2022 Blind loop.

design.title: Design a movie ticketing platform
design.prompt: BookMyShow/Fandango-style ticketing: browse, select seats, pay.
probes: seat-level concurrency and double-booking prevention
traffic spikes for hot releases
APIs, schema, caching, async processes, global/multi-region design
design.evidence: Design round (Hire rating) of the 2024 London senior loop.

design.title: Operations at scale: find and fix the bottleneck
design.prompt: Discussion round: how do you detect bottlenecks in a live system and remedy them?
probes: load balancers, LB access logs, multi-region LB and regional routing
slow-query detection, DB load analysis, master-slave replication lag
IaC (Terraform) and multi-region deployment
splitting a monolith into microservices — HLD first, then 'how do you actually do it in cloud'
design.evidence: Round 4 of the Aug 2024 Bengaluru SSE loop.

design.title: Design a message queue / distributed event log (Kafka-like)
design.prompt: Design a message queue or append-only event log with producers, consumers and retention — Confluent's 'signature' domain question.
probes: topics, partitions, consumer offsets and replay
replication with leader/follower; what happens when a node dies mid-write
delivery guarantees: at-most/at-least/exactly-once and the real cost of exactly-once (idempotent consumers usually suffice)
ordering within vs across partitions; partition key choice
retention, durability-vs-latency acks trade-off
design.evidence: Named the signature Confluent design question by prep guides (DesignGurus, TechInterview); 'design a Spotify-like service' and metrics/streaming prompts in candidate reports orbit the same material; no 2024-26 candidate report of the literal prompt found, likely because many sign NDAs.

design.title: Design a reliable event-ingestion pipeline for out-of-order records
design.prompt: Ingest a high-volume event stream where records arrive late/out of order; make downstream views correct and timely.
probes: event time vs processing time, watermarks, late-record policy
exactly-once vs at-least-once with idempotent sinks
partitioning and backpressure
replayability
design.evidence: Cited as a recent candidate-reported question by TechPrep's 2026 Confluent guide.

design.title: Design a distributed feature-flag / config propagation system
design.prompt: Propagate feature flags/config changes to thousands of microservice instances quickly and safely.
probes: push vs poll, fanout, caching and TTLs
consistency window and kill-switch latency
versioning, rollback, audit
design.evidence: Cited as a recent candidate-reported question by TechPrep's 2026 Confluent guide.

design.title: Design a user-notification system at large scale
design.prompt: Deliver notifications (push/email/in-app) to users of a large application.
probes: fanout and rate limiting per provider
retries, idempotency, dedup
user preferences and batching
design.evidence: Listed under Confluent on Dataford's question bank (surfaced in search; page rate-limited during research).

design.title: Design a Spotify-like music streaming service
design.prompt: High-level design of a music streaming product.
probes: catalog/metadata vs audio blob storage
CDN and playback
playlists/follows feed
design.evidence: Oct 2022 Blind loop (junior role, 'standard' design round); older one-off.

lld.title: Job/task scheduler with concurrency
lld.prompt: Design and code a scheduler that runs submitted jobs/tasks across worker threads: schedule(task, time/delay or dependencies), bounded workers, safe shutdown. Write real or pseudo-code with mutexes/semaphores/condition variables and reason about races.
lld.deliverable: Working code or detailed pseudocode in a shared IDE; single-threaded correctness first, then thread safety
probes: mutex vs semaphore choice (one campus interviewer insisted on semaphores)
waking the right worker when the next deadline changes
starvation, fairness, graceful shutdown
what the concurrency primitives actually guarantee
lld.round: Concurrency round (dedicated through ~2023; now mostly folded into coding rounds as follow-ups)
lld.evidence: Blind Sep 2022 onsite ('design task scheduler'); Oct 2022 Blind loop ('design and code a problem to schedule jobs'); Aug 2023 campus pure-concurrency round (semaphore pseudocode); 2024-25 reports show concurrency only as follow-ups, and an Apr 2025 commenter's loop had no dedicated round.

lld.title: Random queue with multiset equality, RLE and thread safety
lld.prompt: Implement a queue whose dequeue returns a uniformly random stored element. Then: how do you test that two such queues hold the same multiset (ignoring order/layout)? What synchronization does a multithreaded version need? Finally, if contents are stored run-length-encoded as (value,count) pairs, compare two RLE queues for multiset equality WITHOUT expanding runs (counts up to 1e12, up to 2e5 runs, same value may span several runs).
lld.deliverable: Working class implementation plus the RLE-equality function, with a testing discussion
